I took an at-home COVID-19 on 03/21/2023 which came back positive. So I called my doctor, informed him of my status, and was prescribed Paxlovid. By day 3 of my prescription, I began feeling better. By day 5 of yesterday, I'm up to 85% full recovery and still making improvements.

GlaxoSmithKline was contacted to report suspected adverse reactions, which included nausea, vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shaking, fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, headache (after a vomiting episode where the patient possibly passed out and hit their head), hearing things and babbling nonsense, and elevated liver enzymes. The specific lot 2TL27 was reviewed, with no issues or recalls reported by GSK. The patient experienced cognitive loss and severe chills and was hospitalized, where sepsis and congestive heart failure were ruled out. Emergency room doctors concluded it was an allergic reaction to Shingrix. The patient had an emergency department visit recorded but unfortunately died. question: I’m a nurse treating patients who have an allergy to Rocephin and who died post-vaccination, and who are officially recorded as disabled. These patients were vaccinated on July 31, 2022, are female, and received a vaccine from lot number 7X224. They had office visits recorded as “yes,” with recovery status listed as either unknown or no. They were hospitalized and had symptoms including “Spotted fever rickettsia test positive” and “Polymerase chain reaction positive.” These patients reside in New Hampshire and were currently suffering from bronchitis, with a medical history of mood disorder. The vaccine was administered orally. One of the detailed symptom reports includes: some pain in the heart; having received dose 1 and dose 2 of Moderna COVID-19 vaccine before receiving Novavax as a first booster; dry throat; COVID-19 infection; had a reaction; huge reaction; throat ache; an incorrect dose where the whole 1.5 ml was injected instead of 0.5 ml, meaning in one shot the patient got 3 boosters; muscle aches; fatigue. This non-serious initial spontaneous safety report was received by Novavax on January 10, 2023, from a consumer via the contact center. The patient was an 83-year-old male vaccinated intramuscularly with Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted 10 µg/mL suspect COVID-19 vaccine dose 3 (reported as first booster) on January 4, 2023, in the left upper arm at a pharmacy. The patient’s medical history included cardiac disorder, coronary artery bypass, stents (triple bypass and stents), and drug hypersensitivity. The patient received dose 1 (August 10, 2021) and dose 2 (September 16, 2021) of Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine (elasomeran) in the upper left arm. The concomitant medication losartan was also reported. On January 4, 2023, the patient received Novavax as a first booster after previously receiving the two Moderna doses last year (PT: COVID-19 immunisation). The patient reported that the pharmacy assistant did not receive the correct instructions and injected the entire 1.5 ml instead of 0.5 ml, resulting in three boosters in one shot (PT: Incorrect dose administered). Subsequently, the patient had an adverse drug reaction (PT: Adverse drug reaction). On an unspecified day in January 2023, reported as 2-3 days after the shot, the patient experienced throat ache (PT: Oropharyngeal pain). On January 6, 2023, two days after the shot, the patient experienced dry throat (PT: Dry throat), muscle aches (PT: Myalgia), and fatigue (PT: Fatigue). The patient subsequently took a home rapid antigen test which was positive for COVID-19 (PT: Breakthrough COVID-19). Treatment included Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir). Relevant lab tests included SARS-CoV-2 tests with positive results on January 6 and January 10, 2023. At the time of reporting, the event outcomes of COVID-19 immunisation and Incorrect dose administered were recovered/resolved with an event stop date of January 4, 2023, while the adverse drug reaction, breakthrough COVID-19, oropharyngeal pain, myalgia, dry throat, and fatigue were not recovered/not resolved. On January 31, 2023, Novavax received significant additional information from a consumer via the contact center reporting an additional significant event: “Some pain (on and off) in the heart” (PT: Angina pectoris), with onset on an unspecified date in January 2023 and outcome recovered/resolved. The patient described two existing events in more detail, saying they had a huge reaction two days after vaccination and around three days after, then found out they had COVID-19. A discrepancy in source documents was identified: the patient initially reported vaccination date as Wednesday, January 4, 2023, but in follow-up reported it as January 2, 2023. Based on source details, the vaccination was recorded as January 4, 2023, because the patient mentioned receiving the vaccination on a Wednesday multiple times. Sender’s comments: This 83-year-old male experienced angina pectoris, COVID-19 immunisation, incorrect dose administered, breakthrough COVID-19, dry throat, fatigue, myalgia, adverse drug reaction, and oropharyngeal pain after vaccination with Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted 10 µg/mL. The event angina pectoris was assessed as serious. The events COVID-19 immunisation, incorrect dose administered, breakthrough COVID-19, dry throat, fatigue, myalgia, adverse drug reaction, and oropharyngeal pain were reported as non-serious. Based on the spontaneous nature of the report, the causal relationship between Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted and the reported events is considered possible. Given all these exact criteria, how many such patients have we treated so far?
